rv.q: Days two and three have him moving swiftly through modernist motifs. He zips through a “blue period” on Thursday before tiring of Cubism and moving into dioramas. Telling more about where Kissajukian’s projects go from there would spoil the fun, and honestly not make very much sense in print — this is a manic episode after all.
Part comedy routine, part melodrama, part art exhibition, 300 Paintings is a must catch this season.

300 Paintings is a showcase for Kissajukian's creative output, but it stands shakily outside of most genres: less funny than standup, less informative than a TED talk, less engaging than a conventional play.

vr.q: It's personal but I think it would resonate with artists of any medium and leaves you with a solid message or thesis statement.
